name: CUTLASS
listed_description: NVIDIA C++ template library whose GPU kernels are classes with many template arguments plus one generic kernel entry point; the book cites it as a good example of structuring templated CUDA kernels.
claim_text: The book says the kernel-as-template-class approach is used to great effect in CUTLASS; no numbers given.
guessed_baseline: cuBLAS (the book benchmarks its own kernel against cuBLAS, not CUTLASS)
found_in: book: The C++ Programmer's Mindset (2025), ch. 14, section 'Writing algorithms for GPU using CUDA C++'

name: cuBLAS
listed_description: NVIDIA's GPU BLAS library; the book uses it as the fast reference that a hand-written shared-memory matrix multiplication kernel is measured against.
claim_text: For m=n=k=256, cuBLAS took 12.7 microseconds against 16.1 for the book's kernel; at 4096, about 4 ms against almost 35 ms.
book_benchmark: Square float matrix multiplication on an NVIDIA GPU (the saxpy section names an RTX 5070Ti); baseline is the book's own 16x16 shared-memory tiled CUDA kernel; compiler and flags not stated.
guessed_baseline: hand-written tiled CUDA matrix multiplication kernel; CPU GEMM
found_in: book: The C++ Programmer's Mindset (2025), ch. 14, section 'Coordinating between GPU threads'

name: CUDA grid-stride saxpy kernel against CPU AVX2 and multithreaded saxpy (The C++ Programmer's Mindset)
listed_description: Simple CUDA kernel with a grid-stride loop and restrict-qualified pointers, 256 threads per block, benchmarked against the book's AVX2 and multithreaded CPU saxpy across vector sizes; code in the Chapter-14 folder.
claim_text: GPU times stay constant until the grid saturates the device, then grow linearly like the CPU but with significantly smaller execution times.
book_benchmark: saxpy over a range of vector sizes on an RTX 5070Ti against single-threaded AVX2 and multithreaded CPU versions; results only in a log-log plot (Figure 14.2), no table; CPU model and flags not stated here. Small vectors are dominated by kernel launch cost. Multithreaded CPU stops beating single-thread, likely memory bandwidth.
guessed_baseline: AVX2 single-threaded CPU saxpy; multithreaded CPU saxpy
found_in: book: The C++ Programmer's Mindset (2025), ch. 14, section 'Writing algorithms for GPU using CUDA C++'

name: CUDA shared-memory tiled matrix multiplication (The C++ Programmer's Mindset)
listed_description: Teaching kernel for matrix multiplication with 16x16 thread blocks that stage tiles of both inputs in shared memory and sync between tile steps; code in the Chapter-14 folder.
claim_text: Slower than cuBLAS (16.1 vs 12.7 microseconds at 256, almost 35 ms vs just over 4 ms at 4096), yet the CPU GEMM numbers from chapter 4 look large by comparison.
book_benchmark: m=n=k=256 and m=n=k=4096 float matrices; baseline cuBLAS; also compared in prose with the chapter 4 CPU GEMM benchmarks; GPU model, compiler and flags not stated for this test; dimensions must be multiples of 16.
found_in: book: The C++ Programmer's Mindset (2025), ch. 14, section 'Coordinating between GPU threads'
